title: Upgrades, Downgrades and Spend-Led Tier Moves on a Circle Membership
content:
## Moving a Circle membership between tiers

An upgrade of a Northbeam Circle Membership takes effect on the day it is asked for: the difference in
annual dues is billed as a proration over the whole unused months of the current term, and the new tier's
parameters apply from that day to every benefit not yet redeemed.

A downgrade takes effect at the end of the current term, the current tier's parameters stand until then,
and no dues are refunded for the unused part of the term on a downgrade.

## Migrations that are not migrations

A migration between a consumer tier and a business tier is not a migration but a fresh enrolment, because
the entry gate differs on account type.

## Standings that limit a migration

A membership standing in grace may be upgraded only after the outstanding dues are settled, and a lapsed
membership cannot be migrated at all.

## Moving up on spend rather than on request

A profile whose trailing-term qualifying spend reaches the tier's qualifying spend figure is moved up
without a proration being billed. The trailing-term qualifying spend is the spend the points were earned
on, totalled over the earning occasions falling in the current membership term, from the first day of that
term to its last day inclusive.

## Seats on the tier moved to

Household or business seats above the new tier's allowance are removed as part of the migration, oldest
seat first.

## Cases on the two directions

A member on Circle Plus Annual, whose annual dues are 49.99, upgrading to Circle Total Household Annual,
whose annual dues are 219.99, with 5 whole unused months standing in the term, is billed a proration of the
difference in annual dues over those 5 months, and the benefits of the new tier become available on that
day. The same member asking
instead to move down waits until the end of the current term, keeps the parameters of the tier paid for
until then, and is paid nothing back for the part of the term not used. A member whose trailing-term
qualifying spend has reached the higher tier's qualifying spend figure moves up with no proration billed
at all.
